where: Harness sidebar density and question-tool usage
what: Andrew requested one-line tabs after seeing two-line agent rows, and showed a casual question rendered as plain assistant text rather than the question UI.
cost: Rows consumed too much vertical space, and a working question API was not used in casual conversation.
cause: The layout added a second line to fit metadata, and the prompt scoped ask guidance to task clarification rather than every question expecting an answer.
class: A presentation or tool-use policy misses the actual interaction preference or a common use case.
prevention: One-line rows use compact controls and put numeric context details in the tooltip/popover. The always-on goals note explicitly requires await ask for casual questions, follow-ups and requests to ask a question, with a free-text example; API discovery repeats that policy.
workaround: Existing provider processes must resume under the updated daemon prompt to receive the instruction.
fix: Restored fixed-height one-line rows and compact context rings; strengthened the common launch note and ask help. Native scene tests, offscreen rendering and kernel ask-wait checks validate the controls/API; model compliance remains a prompt policy.
